headline: gas is at a new high for this run, and next year is still rising faster than this winter
commentary: UK power spot is 170.22 £/MWh, up 1.2% since our update on 16 October and 109% above where it was a year ago. It eased after touching 173.79 on 13 October but has not given that back. The gas front month, November, is 223.85 p/therm, up 2.7% since 16 October and about 7.8% above September's peak, a new high for this run. Market reporting this week points to record-low European gas storage going into winter and the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which locks in around 20% of global LNG supply. The Dutch gas benchmark hit its highest level since December 2022 on Tuesday. Forecasters expect a mild, wet winter in Europe, but warn that a cold, still spell in late January could push prices much higher. Once again next year rose faster than this winter: November to March are up 1.9 to 2.8%, Summer 27 4.3%, Winter 27 4.7% and Summer 28 4.1%. A mild forecast has not brought the curve down, so waiting for a warm winter has not paid. A 12-month contract starting in November is about 0.41 p/kWh higher on a wholesale-equivalent basis than on 16 October. A 24-month is up about 0.40 p/kWh and still sits around 16% below the 12-month, so term still buys a lower average price. Waiting has now cost money in all four updates since late September. Day-ahead prices this week ran from £86.94/MWh to £192.98, the swing and the level a fixed price takes off the table.

gas.note: NBP front month Nov 26 is 223.85 p/therm, up 2.7% on its 16 Oct print of 217.90 and about 7.8% above September's peak, a new high for this run. The rest of this winter: Dec 26 225.95, Jan 27 227.19, Feb 27 226.00, Mar 27 214.00, Q1 27 223.50. Again the back of the curve rose faster than the front: the winter months are up 1.9 to 2.8%, against Summer 27 171.58 (+4.3%), Winter 27 163.60 (+4.7%) and Summer 28 101.50 (+4.1%). So the step down from this winter narrowed again: Q1 27 to Winter 27 is a 26.8% discount, from 28.5% on 16 Oct. A rise across the whole curve means a longer contract does not dodge the increase, but it still blends this winter down with cheaper years.
